With 5.42% net margin (1067 tokens on 19691), modest variation in actual LLM response length (reasoning, tool formatting, longer URLs) could reverse C3 outcome.

required_fixes.description: Decision_rule C3 defines total workflow cost as selection + resolution + browser + verification, but producer measures only selection+resolution (browser/verification omitted per spec 5.1 'can be skipped if decisive'). Omission is disclosed but claim_ceiling in report.md is phrased as end-to-end workflow savings. Browser/verification may dominate cost and could cancel 1067-token saving; they are assumed constant across conditions without evidence on this corpus.

required_fixes.fix: Bound claim to 'model token cost (selection+resolution only)' not 'total workflow cost'. If end-to-end claim is intended, measure browser interactions and verification calls on a sampled subset or justify constancy with paired execution traces.

required_fixes.description: COLD (no registry) baseline is 77.34 tokens/task vs ~600 tokens/task for literal/parameterized (8x cheaper). Producer reports this but dismisses as 'different workflow paradigm' without measuring COLD success rate or retrieval cost. At face value, mechanism reuse adds ~500 tokens/task overhead vs generating URL from task goal, undermining product consequence for C-PRODUCT-ECON token economics. The 5.42% param vs literal saving is negligible compared to 87% penalty vs cold.

required_fixes.fix: Measure COLD success rate with real model URL generation and include retrieval-failure/repair cost. Report full economics: registry vs cold, not only literal vs param. State explicitly that token savings vs literal do not imply savings vs no-registry baseline.

validity_findings.finding: Resolution tokens vary 0-122 (avg 65.7 for slotted tasks). Tasks with 0 slots (admin-view-user 1-5, blog-list-posts, shop-list-categories, admin-list-users, auth-me) have 0 resolution cost and thus largest net savings (~99 tokens). Tasks with heavy query-param slots (search-shop 122 tokens, pm-create-task 108, pm-view-project 106) incur overhead that exceeds selection saving on 6 tasks, making param more expensive individually. Aggregate 5.42% saving is driven by 0-slot tasks, not by sharing frequency alone.

validity_findings.finding: PM view-project template is malformed: literal /orgs/org-100/projects/proj-200 inferred as /orgs/${item_0}/project${item_1}00 (missing 's' in projects, trailing '00' literal). N=32 is deterministic population, not sample; no variance, CI, or significance test reported. 5.42% is population arithmetic for this synthetic corpus, not an estimate. Claim cannot be generalized to larger registries or different sharing distributions without replication.

claim_ceiling: On the frozen synthetic 32-task corpus (6 domains, 32 literal vs 25 parameterized mechanisms via heuristic regex, 0.858 storage dedup ratio) with analytical tiktoken cl100k_base counting and hard-coded completion estimates (2 tokens selection, ~92 token resolution prompts +15 completion), parameterized model token cost (selection+resolution only, browser/verification omitted, no LLM executed, 100% success assumed) is 18624 vs 19691 tokens (5.42% saving, 1067 tokens). Selection saving 3168 tokens (16.09% from smaller registry) exceeds resolution overhead 2101 tokens (10.67%). Saving is driven by 9 zero-slot tasks (0 resolution cost); 6/32 tasks are individually more expensive under parameterized (search-shop +3.76%). COLD (no registry) is 2475 tokens total (77/task), 8x cheaper than either registry condition, but its success rate unmeasured. No evidence for end-to-end workflow cost (browser/verification/retrieval), real SPIDER registry, kernel distill_parameterized(), or production task distribution. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS; C-PARAM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL at synthetic analytical ceiling. Do not promote to product.
